d: Explains how to use appearance modifiers to customize basic user interface objects.
h:
import BetaAlert from '../includes/beta-features/beta-alert.md'

By utilizing appearance modifiers, you can further customize the appearance of your GuiObjects.

  • Apply a gradient to the background of an object.
  • Apply a stroke to text or a border.
  • Set rounded corners for an object.
  • Increase padding between the borders of an object.
  • Add a drop shadow behind an object.

Gradient

The UIGradient object applies a color and transparency gradient to its parent GuiObject.

    <img src="../assets/ui/ui-objects/UIGradient-Example.png" width="480" />

<div class="gcell" markdown="1">
    <img src="../assets/studio/explorer/UIGradient.png" width="320" />

You can configure the gradient by:

  • Setting its colors through a ColorSequence in the gradient's Color property.
  • Setting its transparency through a NumberSequence in the gradient's Transparency property.
  • Choosing the gradient's type through the Type property.
  • Choosing the gradient's starting point (inside or outside the parent's bounds) through the Offset property.
  • Choosing the gradient's angle through the Rotation property.
  • Choosing the gradient's scale through the Scale property.
  • Choosing the gradient's edge sampling behavior through the TileMode property.

Color sequence

To set a gradient's color sequence:

  1. In the Explorer window, select the UIGradient.
  2. In the Properties window, click inside the Color property field, then click the ⋯ button to the right of the input box.

  1. Each triangle on the bottom axis of the color sequence is a keypoint that determines the color value at that point.

1. Click a keypoint in the color sequence to select or reposition it, or add another keypoint by clicking anywhere on the graph. 2. Click the small square next to Color to open the Colors pop-up window, then select the desired color for the keypoint. 3. If needed, repeat these steps to add/adjust colors across the graph.

Transparency

To adjust a gradient's transparency across its range:

  1. In the Explorer window, select the UIGradient.
  2. In the Properties window, click inside the Transparency property field, then click the ⋯ button to the right of the input box.

  1. Each square across the number sequence graph is a keypoint that determines the transparency value at that point.

1. Click a keypoint in the number sequence to select or reposition it, or add another keypoint by clicking anywhere on the graph. 2. Enter a specific time/value combination through the Time and Value inputs. 3. If needed, repeat these steps to add/adjust transparency levels across the graph.

Type

Beta: this feature is still being tested by Roblox and may change.

A gradient's Type property sets its type from among Linear, Radial, Elliptical, or Conical.

  • Linear — The color/transparency sequence transitions in a straight line across the element. The direction is controlled by its rotation and the position by its offset. This is the default.

  • Radial — The color/transparency sequence radiates outward from the element's center, optionally shifted by Offset. The radius is defined by the average of the element's width and height divided by two, effectively $\text{(width+height)/4}$. Rotation has no effect on a radial gradient.

  • Elliptical — The color/transparency sequence radiates outward from the element's center in an ellipse, optionally shifted by Offset. The ellipse's horizontal and vertical radii are half the element's width and height, so the ellipse fits the element's bounds. Rotation rotates the ellipse's axes.

  • Conical — The color/transparency sequence sweeps clockwise around the center of the element, optionally shifted by Offset. Rotation controls the starting and ending angle of the sweep. By default this sweeps from 0 to 360 degrees, but Scale values less than 1 can reduce that angle.

Offset and rotation

The Offset and Rotation properties let you adjust the gradient's control points and its angle. As illustrated in the following diagrams, Offset is based on a percentage of the parent's width or height, and both positive or negative values are valid.

<figure>
<img src="../assets/ui/ui-objects/UIGradient-Offset-X-0.png" width="376" />
<figcaption>Offset.X = `0`</figcaption>

<figure>
<img src="../assets/ui/ui-objects/UIGradient-Offset-X-Pos-0.25.png" width="376" />
<figcaption>Offset.X = `0.25`</figcaption>

<figure>
<img src="../assets/ui/ui-objects/UIGradient-Offset-X-Neg-0.25.png" width="376" />
<figcaption>Offset.X = `-0.25`</figcaption>

Similarly, when you rotate the gradient, the control points also rotate:

Scale

Beta: this feature is still being tested by Roblox and may change.

A gradient's Scale multiplies the extent of the gradient, controlling how much of the color/transparency sequence is visible within the element.

  • When Scale is less than 1, the gradient spans less than the full extent. The remaining color/transparency is filled in according to the TileMode property.

  • When Scale is greater than 1, the gradient spans more than the full extent and only a part of the color/transparency is visible.

  • For Elliptical gradients, Scale affects both radii of the ellipse.

Tile Mode

Beta: this feature is still being tested by Roblox and may change.

The TileMode property sets how the gradient repeats when the full sequence does not fully cover the parent element.

  • Clamp — Default mode where the color/transparency values at the start and end of the sequence extend infinitely, so the start values fill any area before the gradient and the end values fill any area after it.

  • Repeat — The gradient repeats by wrapping the color/transparency sequence tiles seamlessly from end back to start. This can produce a visible seam if the first and last color/transparency values in the sequence differ.

  • Mirror — The gradient reflects at each boundary so the color/transparency sequence ping‑pongs. This produces a smooth repetition with no seam, since the direction reverses at each tile edge.

Stroke

The UIStroke instance applies an outline to text or a border. Key features include:

  • Adjustable color and thickness of the stroke outline.
  • Ability to set the stroke transparency independently of the parent's transparency.
  • Customizable position and/or offset relative to the parent's border.
  • Three corner styles (round, bevel, or miter).
  • Stroke gradient support through the UIGradient instance.

Thickness

You can set the stroke width through the Thickness property which is measured in pixels (default) or scaled relative to the parent, depending on the modifier's StrokeSizingMode. If stroke is on text and StrokeSizingMode is set to ScaledSize, thickness is relative to the font size.

Avoid tweening the Thickness property of a UIStroke instance applied to text objects. This renders and stores many glyph sizes each frame, potentially causing performance issues or text flickering.

Color or gradient

You can set the stroke color through the Color property, as well as insert a child UIGradient instance to create gradient strokes.

Both the parent object and UIStroke can have child UIGradient instances, letting you set gradients on the stroke and fill independently.

Text outline or border

Depending on its parent type, UIStroke operates as either a text outline or as a border. When you parent UIStroke to a text object like TextLabel, it applies to the text's outline; when you parent UIStroke to other GuiObjects, it applies to the border.

When applied to a text object, you can override the default stroke behavior by the ApplyStrokeMode property, letting you apply the stroke to the object's bounds instead of the text itself. You can even control the text outline and border independently by parenting two UIStroke instances to a text object, one set to Contextual and the other to Border.

Border position/offset

BorderStrokePosition sets the stroke's position relative to its parent's border and BorderOffset lets you specify an additional offset to the stroke's position.

<figure>
<img src="../assets/ui/ui-objects/UIStroke-BorderStrokePosition-Center.png" width="312" />
<figcaption>BorderStrokePosition = Center</figcaption>
</figure>
<figure>
<img src="../assets/ui/ui-objects/UIStroke-BorderStrokePosition-Inner.png" width="312" />
<figcaption>BorderStrokePosition = Inner</figcaption>
</figure>
<figure>
<img src="../assets/ui/ui-objects/UIStroke-BorderStrokePosition-Outer.png" width="312" />
<figcaption>BorderStrokePosition = Outer</figcaption>
</figure>

<figure>
<img src="../assets/ui/ui-objects/UIStroke-BorderOffset-Out.png" width="312" />
<figcaption>BorderOffset = `(0.15, 0)`</figcaption>
</figure>
<figure>
<img src="../assets/ui/ui-objects/UIStroke-BorderOffset-In.png" width="312" />
<figcaption>BorderOffset = `(0, -16)`</figcaption>
</figure>

Transparency

The Transparency property sets the stroke transparency independently of the parent object's BackgroundTransparency or TextTransparency. This allows you to render text and borders that are "hollow" (consisting of only an outline).

Corner style

The LineJoinMode property lets you control how corners are interpreted. It accepts a value of either Round, Bevel, or Miter.

Layering

To layer multiple sibling UIStroke instances on a GuiObject from front to back, you can utilize the ZIndex property. Those with a lower ZIndex render under (behind) those with a higher ZIndex.

Note that the rendering order for UIStroke instances with the same ZIndex is undefined. Do not apply multiple UIStroke instances with the same index if their rendering order matters.

Corners

The UICorner instance applies deformation to the corners of its parent GuiObject. You can control the applied radius through the CornerRadius property using either Scale or Offset.

Scale rounds the corners to a percentage based on the total length of the shortest edge of the parent, meaning that a scale of 0.5 or higher deforms the parent into a "pill" shape, regardless of its width or height. Offset rounds the corners to a specific number of pixels, regardless of the width/height of the parent.

<figure>
<img src="../assets/ui/ui-objects/UICorner-Scale-0.25.png" width="392" />
<figcaption>Scale = `0.25`  ·  Offset = `0`</figcaption>

<figure>
<img src="../assets/ui/ui-objects/UICorner-Scale-0.5.png" width="392" />
<figcaption>Scale = `0.5`  ·  Offset = `0`</figcaption>

<figure>
<img src="../assets/ui/ui-objects/UICorner-Offset-32.png" width="392" />
<center><figcaption>Scale = `0`  ·  Offset = `32`</figcaption></center>

<figure>
<img src="../assets/ui/ui-objects/UICorner-Offset-64.png" width="392" />
<center><figcaption>Scale = `0`  ·  Offset = `64`</figcaption></center>

You can also control individual corners through the TopLeftRadius, TopRightRadius, BottomRightRadius, and BottomLeftRadius properties.

Padding

A UIPadding object applies top, bottom, left, and/or right padding to the contents of the parent GuiObject. For example, you can move the text inside a text label downward or upward by applying an offset to the modifier's PaddingBottom property.

Shadow

A UIShadow object renders a shadow for its parent UI instance. A shadow can follow the parent's rectangular shape or the glyphs of a text object. Shape shadows can appear outside or inside the parent, and mask the area directly behind the parent. Both shape and text shadows can use a color gradient.

If the parent has a UICorner or a nonzero GuiObject.Rotation, its shape shadow follows the same corners or rotation. UIShadow doesn't support Path2D or textures.

Beta: this feature is still being tested by Roblox and may change.

Shape and text shadows

The Mode property determines what casts the shadow, and both modes can coexist under the same parent.

  • Shape is the default. The shadow follows the rectangular area of any GuiObject.
  • Text follows the text glyphs of a TextLabel, TextButton, or TextBox. Other UI objects don't render a shadow in this mode.
<figure>
<img src="../assets/ui/ui-objects/UIShadow-Mode-Shape.png" width="424" />
<figcaption>Mode = Shape</figcaption>

Spread, Inset, and ShowBehindParent have no effect in text mode.

Blur

The BlurRadius property determines the shadow's blurriness. A larger value makes the shadow's edges appear softer. Note that the scale factor of this UDim property is relative to the parent's width or height, whichever is shorter.

<figure>
<img src="../assets/ui/ui-objects/UIShadow-BlurRadius-Scale-0.png" width="424" />
<figcaption>BlurRadius = `(0, 0)`</figcaption>

Color and transparency

The Color property determines the shadow's color, while Transparency sets the shadow's transparency with 0 being fully opaque and 1 being fully transparent.

<figure>
<img src="../assets/ui/ui-objects/UIShadow-Color-White-Transparency-0.6.png" width="424" />
<figcaption>Color = `(255, 255, 255)`  ·  Transparency = `0.6`</figcaption>

For a multicolor shadow, insert a UIGradient as a child of the UIShadow. The gradient affects the shadow without changing the parent's fill.

Offset and spread

The Offset property moves the shadow relative to the parent's position, while Spread expands or shrinks the shadow relative to the parent's size.

<figure>
<img src="../assets/ui/ui-objects/UIShadow-Offset-Offset.png" width="424" />
<figcaption>Offset = `{0, -14}, {0, 6}`</figcaption>

Inset shadows

Set Inset to true to render the shadow on top of and inside the parent instead of behind it. Positive Spread values expand an inset shadow toward the center of the parent.

<figure>
<img src="../assets/ui/ui-objects/UIShadow-Inset-False.png" width="424" />
<figcaption>Inset = `false`</figcaption>

Reveal content behind a transparent parent

By default, ShowBehindParent is true, so the entire shape shadow renders, including the portion directly behind the parent. Set it to false to mask that portion of the shadow. This prevents the shadow from darkening content visible through a transparent parent.

<figure>
<img src="../assets/ui/ui-objects/UIShadow-ShowBehindParent-True.png" width="424" />
<figcaption>ShowBehindParent = `true`</figcaption>

This property has no effect on inset or text shadows.

Layer shadows

Add multiple UIShadow instances to the same parent to combine effects. The ZIndex property controls their render order. Shadows with lower values render behind shadows with higher values.

The render order of shadows that share the same ZIndex is undefined. Assign each sibling shadow a different value when their order matters.

kid.simple: Appearance modifiers are small objects you drop inside a UI element to make it look nicer. `UIGradient` blends colors, `UIStroke` adds an outline, `UICorner` rounds the corners, `UIPadding` adds space inside the edges, and `UIShadow` adds a shadow. You do not need code for any of them; just insert one and change its properties. Mixing them turns plain boxes into polished buttons and panels.
kid.analogy: Modifiers are like accessories for your avatar: the avatar is the same, but adding a hat, an outline glow, or a shadow makes it look totally different.
keyPoints: Each modifier works by being placed inside (as a child of) the UI object it changes.
`UIGradient` blends colors (`Color`) and see-through levels (`Transparency`) across the object; `Rotation` and `Offset` change its direction and starting point.
Gradient `Type` can be Linear, Radial, Elliptical, or Conical, and `Scale` and `TileMode` control how it repeats (these are beta features).
`UIStroke` outlines text when placed in a text object, or outlines the border of other objects; `Thickness`, `Color`, and `Transparency` style it.
`ApplyStrokeMode` set to Border puts the stroke around a text object's box instead of its letters.
`UICorner` rounds corners with `CornerRadius`: scale 0.5 or more makes a pill shape, and offset rounds by a set number of pixels.
`UIPadding` adds space between the edges of an object and its contents, such as pushing text away from a label's edges.
`UIShadow` draws a shadow behind or inside an object, with blur, color, offset, and spread settings.

terms.modifier: An object that changes how its parent looks, without being something you see on its own.
terms.gradient: A smooth blend from one color to another, like a sunset going from orange to purple.
terms.keypoint: A marker on the gradient that says "at this point, use this color". Time 0 is the start, 1 is the end.
terms.ColorSequence / NumberSequence: Lists of keypoints for colors or numbers along a gradient.
terms.stroke: An outline drawn around text or a box.
terms.Thickness: How wide the outline is, in pixels by default. 4 is thin, 12 is chunky.
terms.CornerRadius: How round the corners are. Offset 16 rounds them by 16 pixels; scale 0.5 makes a full pill shape.
terms.padding: Empty space inside the edge. A `PaddingLeft` of 10 pixels moves contents 10 pixels in from the left.
terms.blur: Soft, fuzzy edges. A bigger `BlurRadius` makes a softer shadow.
terms.spread: How much bigger or smaller the shadow is than the object.
terms.beta: A feature still being tested that you may need to turn on in Studio settings.

example.title: Make a fancy rounded button
example.place: LocalScript inside a TextButton (inside a ScreenGui in StarterGui)
example.code:
local button = script.Parent
button.BackgroundColor3 = Color3.new(1, 1, 1) -- start from a plain white button

-- Round the corners by 12 pixels
local corner = Instance.new("UICorner")
corner.CornerRadius = UDim.new(0, 12)
corner.Parent = button

-- Blue-to-purple background blend
local gradient = Instance.new("UIGradient")
gradient.Color = ColorSequence.new(Color3.fromRGB(0, 120, 255), Color3.fromRGB(150, 0, 255))
gradient.Rotation = 90 -- blend from top to bottom
gradient.Parent = button

-- Dark outline around the button's border
local stroke = Instance.new("UIStroke")
stroke.ApplyStrokeMode = Enum.ApplyStrokeMode.Border -- outline the box, not the letters
stroke.Thickness = 3
stroke.Color = Color3.fromRGB(20, 20, 40)
stroke.Parent = button

-- Keep text away from the edges
local padding = Instance.new("UIPadding")
padding.PaddingLeft = UDim.new(0, 10)
padding.PaddingRight = UDim.new(0, 10)
padding.Parent = button
explain: We start from a plain white button.
A `UICorner` rounds the corners by 12 pixels.
A `UIGradient` blends blue into purple, turned 90 degrees so it goes top to bottom.
A `UIStroke` with `ApplyStrokeMode` Border draws a dark outline around the button box instead of the text.
A `UIPadding` keeps the text 10 pixels from the left and right edges.

watchOut: A `UIStroke` inside a `TextLabel` or `TextButton` outlines the letters by default. Set `ApplyStrokeMode` to Border to outline the box.
Do not tween the `Thickness` of a stroke on text. It can cause lag or flickering.
If two strokes or shadows have the same `ZIndex`, their order is random. Give them different values.
Some gradient and shadow features are beta, so they may not work until you enable them.
